question.:question/problem:
Find the antiderivative of $\sqrt[3]{x^{2}}$.

Work on $x>0$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
We start by writing the root as a rational power, $\sqrt[3]{x^{2}}={x}^{2/3}.$ So, we can apply the power rule with $n=\frac{2}{3}$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \sqrt[3]{x^{2}}\,\text{d}x & =\int {x}^{2/3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2/3+1}}{(\frac{2}{3}+1)}+C \\  & =\frac{{x}^{5/3}}{(\frac{5}{3})}+C \\  & =\frac{3{x}^{5/3}}{5}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Again, let's check by differentiating:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{3{x}^{5/3}}{5}+C) & = \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{3{x}^{5/3}}{5})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(C) & = \\ \frac{3}{5}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{5/3})+0 & = \\ \frac{3}{5}\cdot \frac{5}{3}{x}^{5/3-1} & = \\ {x}^{2/3}\,✓\end{aligned}
$$
